target.title: fix(gateway): tighten CSP connect-src from bare ws:/wss: to explicit endpoints
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The Control UI CSP `connect-src` directive used bare scheme sources `ws:` and `wss:`. Per CSP spec, a bare scheme source allows connections to **any** host — meaning any XSS in the Control UI could exfiltrate data via WebSocket to an arbitrary server.

## Why This Change Was Made

Control UI actually only needs three specific WebSocket/connection targets beyond `'self'`:
1. **Gateway WebSocket** — same origin, covered by `'self'`
2. **OpenAI API** — `https://api.openai.com` (already explicitly listed, HTTPS)
3. **Google Gemini Live** — `wss://generativelanguage.googleapis.com` for realtime voice feature (was relying on bare `wss:`)

Rather than allowing "any WebSocket anywhere", the policy now explicitly names each endpoint.

## User Impact

- **No visible change** — all existing functionality works identically
- Defense-in-depth improvement if a future XSS vulnerability is discovered in the Control UI

## Evidence

- ~60 CSP unit tests pass (4 test files, all green)~
- Verified that:
  - `gateway.ts:520` — Gateway WebSocket uses page origin (`'self'`)
  - `realtime-talk-google-live.ts:106` — Google Live WebSocket uses `wss://generativelanguage.googleapis.com` (now explicitly listed)
  - `realtime-talk-webrtc.ts:126` — OpenAI Realtime uses HTTPS `fetch` to `api.openai.com` (already listed)
